title: PIN-01 AC1: service_catalog has no version/status column — "active version"/DEPRECATED concept does not exist in schema
summary: While designing PIN-01 (dependency version resolution at instance start) against the real current schema, found that public.service_catalog (migrations/049_repository_service_catalog.sql, altered only by migrations/GBL-117_svc01_service_catalog_scope.sql) has no version or status column at all -- service_id is the table's PRIMARY KEY, one row per service, not one row per service-version. PIN-01 AC1's trigger condition ("names no catalog entry with an active version") and PIN-03 AC3 ("pinned catalog entry version is set to DEPRECATED") both assume a per-version status this table does not have. src/engine/service_task.zig's resolveCatalogEndpoint() and every other existing caller already treat the catalog as unversioned. This blocks full implementation of PIN-01's catalog_entry resolution branch to its literal AC text; a provisional stopgap interpretation (each row is an implicit single active version, no version history) is documented in src/design/pin-01-dependency-version-resolution.md Open questions #1 but the real schema decision (add version/status columns vs. accept the degenerate single-version reading) needs REQ-ANALYST/ORCH, not a unilateral CODE-DESIGNER call.

root_cause.details: service_catalog was designed (REPO-07/SVC-01) as an unversioned per-service registry. PIN-01/PIN-03, added later in the same requirements set, assume the catalog has version history and per-version lifecycle status (active/DEPRECATED) that was never built.

prevention: REQ-ANALYST/ORCH should decide between widening service_catalog with real version/status columns (breaking reshape of an already-RELEASED table) or formally accepting the single-implicit-version reading before BACKEND-DEV implements PIN-01's catalog_entry resolution branch.

CODE-DESIGNER should flag this class of cross-requirement schema assumption mismatch (a later requirement assuming infrastructure an earlier, already-RELEASED requirement never built) as an explicit Open question rather than silently picking an interpretation, as done here.
